note: Backtest pack for the 2022-10-05 OPEC+ decision (33rd ONOMM). Thesis: the OPEC+ headline cut of 2 million b/d brings an actual supply tightening of about 2 million b/d and pushes Brent higher. Stance is relative to this thesis: supports = backs a link (the cut was announced and is large, prices rose on it, analysts expected a price rebound); contradicts = weakens it (members already producing below quota, so the effective cut is smaller than the headline; observed output fell by less than the headline; Brent ended below the decision-day level); neutral = background only (pre-meeting reports of what would be considered). Excerpts dated on or before 2022-10-05 were public at decision time; later excerpts are outcome data for scoring only and must not enter the model context for this case.

excerpt_notes.op-001: Argus is one of seven secondary sources OPEC+ uses for compliance; Argus's own survey put the August shortfall at 3.41 million bpd.
excerpt_notes.op-006: QCI timestamp 2022-10-05 17:36 +01:00, after the meeting concluded.
excerpt_notes.op-014: Other drivers moved Brent in this window (demand outlook, China COVID policy, the Russian price cap); the fall is not attributable to the cut alone.

excerpts.source: Quantum Commodity Intelligence (T3 trade media, citing Argus and OPEC data) · paragraph 1
excerpts.text: Production from the OPEC+ alliance fell short of its target level in August by a record 3.58 million bpd, according to a report published by Argus Media, one of the producer group's official data suppliers.

excerpts.source: Quantum Commodity Intelligence (T3 trade media, citing OPEC data) · paragraphs 2 and 7
excerpts.text: The coalition's 10 participating core OPEC members accounted for 1.399 million bpd of the August shortfall, while their non-OPEC allies underproduced by 2.185 million bpd, according to OPEC data. … Underproduction from Russia, constrained by western sanctions, but not exempted from its OPEC+ commitments, amounted to 1.252 million bpd in August

excerpts.source: Quantum Commodity Intelligence (T3 trade media, citing a UBS note) · paragraph 1
excerpts.text: Only a cut in OPEC+ production levels of at least 500,000 bpd can stop the current bearish sentiment in crude oil markets, investment bank UBS said in a note on Tuesday.

excerpts.source: Quantum Commodity Intelligence (T3 trade media) · final paragraph
excerpts.text: Analysts said that small increments of 100,000 bpd up or down have little impact on actual production levels given that the group is collectively missing targets by nearly 3 million bpd, although it would send a signal to the market on broader policy.

excerpts.source: Reuters (T2 wire, via BOE Report reprint) · lead
excerpts.text: OPEC+ will consider an oil output cut of more than a million barrels per day (bpd) when it meets on Oct. 5, OPEC sources told Reuters on Sunday. The figure is slightly above estimates for a cut given last week, which ranged between 500,000 bpd and 1 million bpd.

excerpts.source: Quantum Commodity Intelligence (T3 trade media) · paragraphs 1 and 3
excerpts.text: OPEC+ announced Wednesday a production cut of 2 million barrels per day from November, which was at the higher end of market expectations heading into the week. … Dec22 Brent was trading around $93/b shortly after the meeting concluded, up around $8/b from Friday's settle.

excerpts.source: Quantum Commodity Intelligence (T3 trade media, citing a Goldman Sachs investor note) · paragraph 7
excerpts.text: "Due to widespread capacity limits within OPEC+, a headline ("paper") cut is likely to overstate significantly the effective ("physical") curtailment of production. The effective cut is likely to be only circa 50% of the headline quota figures," Goldman Sachs said in an investor note.

excerpts.source: Quantum Commodity Intelligence (T3 trade media) · paragraph 6
excerpts.text: However, in real terms, the total reduction will be around 50% of the headline figure, with most members of the alliance remaining within compliance even at reduced quotas, as the wider group continues to miss the target by over 3.5 million bpd.

excerpts.source: Quantum Commodity Intelligence (T3 trade media, citing UBS) · paragraph 4
excerpts.text: "The OPEC+ cut could help Brent prices rebound to $110/bbl by year-end," said UBS bank, commenting on the size of the cut. The 2 million bpd cut is the largest reduction since the group slashed quotas by 9.7 million bpd at the height of the Covid pandemic in 2020.

excerpts.source: Reuters survey (T2 wire, via Oman Observer reprint) · paragraphs 2 and 4
excerpts.text: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) pumped 29.01 million barrels per day (bpd) this month, the survey found, down 710,000 bpd from October. … Their decision for November called for a 2 million bpd cut in the OPEC+ output target, of which about 1.27 million bpd was meant to come from the 10 participating OPEC countries.

excerpts.source: Reuters survey (T2 wire, via Oman Observer reprint) · paragraphs 6-7
excerpts.text: Output from the 10 members fell by 720,000 bpd month-on-month, the survey found, leaving actual production 800,000 bpd below the group's November output target. … As a result of production being below target, OPEC over-delivered on its pledged cuts with a compliance rate of 163% in November, the survey found.

excerpts.source: Reuters survey (T2 wire, via Oman Observer reprint) · paragraph 9
excerpts.text: In November, Saudi Arabia has cut output by 500,000 bpd versus October, the survey found, virtually all of the pledged amount. The United Arab Emirates and Kuwait made the next largest curbs.
